data.body:
Implemented and superseded by story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 (closed), via ticket 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd — merged 693a6bf41.

Your rule is now the implementation, essentially verbatim. Dependency-link escalation is based on the ticket HIERARCHY, not the ticket type: _TYPE_TIER and its three helpers are deleted.

- "Any two siblings under the same parent may have a dependency relationship" — two direct children of the same parent link exactly as given, whatever their types. A task and a story under one epic now link directly.
- "Dependency links outside of the same parent must escalate to the closest shared parent" — each endpoint escalates to its own ancestor that is a child of the two endpoints nearest common ancestor.
- "Tickets with no parent are considered siblings for this purpose" — implemented as a virtual-root sentinel appended to every ancestor chain, so a common ancestor always exists and there is no undefined disjoint case. Two roots link unchanged; a deep leaf linked across trees escalates to its own root.

Your worked example is a regression test (test_resolve_hierarchy_link_jira_reb_1582_worked_example): with Epic A parenting Task B and Story C, and Task D under Story C, `D depends_on B` escalates to `C depends_on B`, while `B depends_on C` records directly.

One consequence worth recording, since it was the largest behavioural change and was approved deliberately: under the old type-tier rule two leaves in different sub-trees were always "comparable" and linked directly. Under your rule their nearest common ancestor is the shared grandparent, so cousins now escalate to their respective parents. Three existing tests asserted the opposite and were inverted; the other eight held unchanged, which was the main evidence the formulation was right.

Legacy edges already on disk were repaired separately under 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827: 18 found on this tracker, 12 repaired, 8 residual and provably inert (all endpoints closed).

Also recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics: re-parenting a ticket silently invalidates previously-correct links, because comparability is structural. Two NEW mis-escalated edges with OPEN endpoints appeared within hours of the remediation. Your rule is correct; keeping the store consistent with it over time needs re-parent to either auto-remediate or be denied.
